reading: Each of the two isolated cells shoots full-length lines of its own colour along its row and its column to the grid border; the rectangle strictly enclosed by the four lines is filled with colour 1.
verb: draw cross lines and fill enclosed box
why: the lines through both markers span the whole grid; the only background area not touching the border is the box between them, and it becomes 1

reading: Two same-shape pieces touch diagonally. Copies of the piece shape in colour 8 are placed on the perpendicular diagonal: each piece's offset from the pair centre is rotated 90 degrees and tripled (copies clipped at the border).

slots.subject: each diagonal pair of identical colour-3 pieces
slots.placement: piece-centre offsets rotated 90 degrees and scaled by 3

why: every pair gets exactly two colour-8 copies of the piece shape at those positions; input cells unchanged

reading: Several straight lines of different colours cross on a uniform background. Output is a 1xN row listing the line colours from bottom layer to top layer, judged by which colour shows at each crossing.

slots.subject: each straight one-colour line (segments, possibly diagonal)
slots.order: partial order from crossings: the colour visible at a crossing is above the other
slots.output: 1 x (number of lines) row, colours from bottom to top

why: at every crossing the visible colour is later in the output row than the hidden one
invariants: output has one cell per line colour

reading: One plus-shaped object has a unique colour; every other object is a solid square of the main colour. The centre cell of each odd-sized square (1x1, 3x3, 5x5) is recoloured to the plus colour; even squares are unchanged. The plus is erased in pairs 1-2 but kept in pair 3 (unexplained).
verb: mark square centres with odd colour

slots.subject: centre cell of each odd-sided solid square
slots.plus: erased to background in two pairs, kept in one; rule unclear (maybe erased when odd squares <= even squares)

why: exactly the single centre cells of odd-sized squares change, to the plus colour

reading: Grey cells on the top row mark columns and grey cells on the right column mark rows; every crossing of a marked row with a marked column (left of the right column) is filled with colour 2.

new_rows.name: cross
new_rows.datalog:
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
top(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0, maxx(M), X < M.
right(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C), maxx(M), X = M, Y > 0.
cross(Y, X) :- top(X), right(Y).

why: every cell (r, c) with a grey cell at (0, c) and at (r, last column) becomes 2; nothing else changes

reading: Grey (5) shapes contain background holes. Each loose coloured object whose shape exactly matches a hole is moved into that hole; non-matching objects stay where they are.

slots.containers: grey objects with enclosed background holes
slots.subject: coloured objects whose shape equals a hole's shape (up to translation)
slots.rest: other objects kept; vacated cells become background

why: each moved object keeps its shape and colour and exactly fills a hole

reading: Short coloured pieces carry grey (5) connector cells at their ends. The pieces are chained left to right: each piece is shifted so its left connector sits right next to the previous piece's right connector, connectors take their piece's colour, and the grid shrinks in width by the overlaps.

slots.subject: each piece (colour run plus attached 5 cells), in left-to-right order
slots.joint: grey connector cells, recoloured to the piece colour
slots.placement: translate each piece so its left connector abuts the previous piece's right connector
slots.output size: same height, width = sum of piece widths

why: the output is one connected chain with no grey cells, pieces keep their shapes

reading: There are two 2x2 blocks of colour 2 among scattered 8s. Output is a single cell: 8 if the two blocks are joined by a connected path of 8 cells, otherwise 0.

slots.subject: the two 2x2 colour-2 blocks
slots.output: 1x1: 8 if both blocks lie in one connected component, else 0

why: on every pair the answer matches whether the 2-blocks share a component of non-background cells

reading: A triangular arrow has one cell of a different colour at the centre of its base. A line of that colour is drawn from that cell through the arrow's tip direction to the grid border, painting only background cells.
verb: shoot ray from base cell through tip

new_rows.name: oddcell
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
oddcell(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), N = 1.

why: the ray runs in the direction base-to-tip (up, right, down in the three pairs), starts beyond the tip, and reaches the border; arrow cells are not overwritten

reading: The whole foreground shape moves down by one row.
why: every foreground cell moves by the constant offset (+1, 0); shape and colour kept
